findings.claim: MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T> used to throw TypeAccessException for types with no known hash-resistant comparer. It now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default. That is exactly the comparer the UntrustedData protection exists to prevent, so with UntrustedData set, attacker-controlled keys of an unlisted type (e.g. a custom key struct in a Dictionary/HashSet) get a collision-prone comparer. Deserialization then becomes open to hash-collision DoS, and the protection fails open without any error.

receipt_plan.detail: Set MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and call GetEqualityComparer<T>() for a type with no hash-resistant comparer (e.g. a custom struct, or Dictionary<CustomKey,int> deserialization). Assert TypeAccessException is thrown. It fails at head because the default comparer is returned. Also check the existing MessagePackSecurityTests for the unknown-type case.
